scope: Reference plus six sampled frames at0/1/2/3/4/5.125 seconds per video, not continuous audiovisual listening or a new user verdict
models: same-init frozen-H3 prediction loss1, six updates

assessment.staircase: Control and prediction groups retain arm gestures, turns and rear leg curls across original/swapped/zero music. Some leg timing differs, but rich distinct choreography is not established. Both replace the reference yellow top/grey trousers with white-blue sportswear and add a bag.
assessment.red_outfit: Control/prediction mostly share hand-to-mouth, hand behind head and single-arm lift motif. Zero music changes the final gesture without establishing correct-song adherence.
assessment.shop: Mostly stationary single-arm gestures and small shifts. Prediction original has a larger two-arm gesture in one sampled frame, while other conditions remain similar; no reliable song-specific dance increment is established.
assessment.visual_quality: No obvious catastrophic corruption in inspected frames; no quantified sharpness equivalence or continuous quality acceptance is claimed.

limitations: Six updates over three training references is a feasibility and initial-effect probe, not convergence or a definitive negative result for prediction supervision.
The one heldout prediction MSE improves3.52 percent versus control and0.96 percent versus initialization, but one reference/noise/time cannot establish generalization or music-to-dance quality.
The full200 representation validation has correct-over-first-wrong fraction50.5 percent for both models.
Each music variant uses its own predicted length and packed layout; video differences do not isolate content semantics.
Condition VJP and actual backbone updates prove training connectivity, not useful choreography.
